changes: Implemented Lattice CLI 0.3.5 rollout productization: lattice is now the primary user-facing command, koala remains an explicit legacy alias, rollout_check scans multiple projects with read-only per-project status and nextAction output, docs and prompts now publish lattice-first refresh/check/doctor/session guidance, and smoke tests cover alias compatibility plus rollout scope safety.
usage: Use lattice --version, koala --version for legacy alias verification, lattice check, lattice doctor --format=json, and lattice rollout_check --projects=/path/a,/path/b --json to audit project rollout state. Use lattice session_brief and lattice validate for story lifecycle work.
expectedOutcome: Users see Lattice CLI 0.3.5 as the official CLI entry, koala clearly labeled as legacy compatibility, and rollout_check JSON that reports schema, readOnly=true, macAppRequired=false, summary counts, per-project status, evidence, and nextAction.
actualTranscript: Validation passed via lattice validate --story=B-fd03 --json, npm test fallback passed, verification intent coverage is 12/12, all REVIEW lanes passed, and real-project rollout transcript records conservative warn/fail diagnostics with actionable nextAction values instead of claiming all projects are clean.
outcomeDiff: No product gap. The only intentional difference is that real-project rollout output is conservative: warn/fail drift is surfaced honestly rather than converted into pass.
limitations: rollout_check is a read-only diagnostic and does not apply repairs; external project warnings still require the operator to run project-local check/apply/doctor actions. Mac app is not required for this CLI plus server-authority receipts path.
pitfalls: F-009 caught an acceptance-text mismatch that still promised fixed pass outcomes; it was corrected to match the conservative transcript. Review also caught trailing-comma project parsing and stale koala help text, both now covered by smoke tests.
